messages:
Jordan: Acme support case — SSO started failing right after their IdP cert rotation. Our logs show 'InvalidSignature' in saml verifier. They say it started at ~15:10 PST. Anyone seen this pattern?

Priya: Can you paste the SAMLResponse error snippet and the IdP metadata they sent? Even a small xml excerpt helps.

Jordan: Pasting the relevant parts from the ticket (redacted cert):

--- idp metadata snippet ---
<md:EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme.internal">
  <md:IDPSSODescriptor>
    <md:KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <ds:KeyInfo>
        <ds:X509Data>
          <ds:X509Certificate>MIIC...REDACTED...Q==</ds:X509Certificate>
        </ds:X509Data>
      </ds:KeyInfo>
    </md:KeyDescriptor>
    <md:SingleSignOnService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect" Location="https://idp.acme.internal/sso/redirect"/>
  </md:IDPSSODescriptor>
  <md:AssertionConsumerService index="0" Location="https://app.redwood.ai/acs?relayState=project+123%2B%22quote%22"/>
</md:EntityDescriptor>
--- end snippet ---

Jordan: The SAMLResponse signedinfo shows SignatureMethod rsa-sha256. Customer attached the raw samlresponse; our verifier rejects it with 'signature verification failed (xmlsec error: invalid canonicalization digest)'.

Nate: Two quick suspects: 1) IdP rotated cert but their metadata (or CDN in front of it) changed XML canonicalization or inserted whitespace/line endings that break our strict xmlsec path. 2) The ACS URL contains encoded characters (plus and encoded quote) — if their relayState rewriting proxy decodes differently we can get an audience/recipient mismatch.

Eve: Customer's application logs: "AudienceRestriction failed: expected 'https://app.redwood.ai' got 'https://app.redwood.ai:443'" — so port suffix mismatch on SP entityID. That plus the weird ACS query encoding could explain failures in many clients.

Priya: Jordan — can you run these repro commands and paste outputs?

--- repro commands ---
# fetch metadata and show canonicalized form
curl -fsS https://idp.acme.internal/metadata.xml | xmllint --exc-c14n - | head -n 40

# compute certificate thumbprint they claim matches 'MIIC...'
curl -fsS https://idp.acme.internal/metadata.xml | xmllint --exc-c14n - | sed -n 's/.*<ds:X509Certificate>\(.*\)<\/ds:X509Certificate>.*/\1/p' | base64 -d | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | base64
--- end ---

Jordan: Ran the commands — metadata canonicalization shows their CDN adds a comment node and normalizes line endings, which changes the c14n output compared to the file they uploaded to our ticket. Thumbprint computed from live metadata != thumbprint in their uploaded file.

Nate: That confirms it. Two remediation tracks: (A) Ask IdP to re-publish metadata without the CDN comment/with identical canonicalization; purge CDN caches. (B) Add a tolerant fallback path in our SAML verifier to accept certs based on parsed X509Subject or raw certificate equivalence instead of byte-for-byte c14n match — short-term toggle for this tenant only.

Priya: Also ask them to normalize SP entityID (remove explicit :443) and ensure their ACS proxies don't double-decode '+' vs '%2B' vs ' ' in relayState. Provide example curl to POST SAMLResponse to our ACS to test.

Jordan: Notified customer with step-by-step: 1) re-publish metadata (no injected comments), 2) purge CDN, 3) confirm SP entityID without port, 4) send fresh metadata file to support.

SupportBot: Incident created: INC-2026-745, priority P2, owners: @eng-security and @eng-sso.

Nate: I've created a minimal repro harness in eng-oncall's sso-repro repo using their metadata and our verifier. File: /eng-oncall/sso-repro/acme-metadata-test.xml. Steps documented in the repo README. I'll open a PR to add a temporary tolerant verification flag gated by tenant id.

Eve: Will need eng-security's review for security implications of tolerant verification. Tagging them now.

Priya: Agreed. Please do not enable tenant toggle globally. We will prefer fixing metadata + CDN purge. If customer can't coordinate rotation quickly, toggle can be used as an emergency last resort.

Jordan: Customer acknowledged and will coordinate with IdP ops. I'll update the ticket when they confirm the CDN purge and re-uploaded metadata. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
